headline: Around 50 injured as student wings clash at Jagannath University
summary: Leaders and activists of JCD, Shibir, and Jatiya Chhatra Shakti clashed on campus, leaving several student leaders and journalists injured.
details: Leaders and activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD), Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir, and Jatiya Chhatra Shakti clashed at Jagannath University (JnU) today, leaving around 50 people injured, including student leaders and journalists.
The clash broke out around 11:30 am during a documentary screening program attended by University Grants Commission (UGC) Chairman Prof Dr Mamun Ahmed.

The violence started when JCD activists stopped JnUCSU representatives and members of Inquilab Mancha from entering the venue with placards demanding better campus facilities and army oversight of the second campus construction.
Injured individuals include JnUCSU Vice-President Riazul Islam, General Secretary Abdul Alim Arif, Jatiya Chhatra Shakti President Shahin Mia, and JCD leader Yasin Saif.

Abdul Alim Arif alleged that JCD activists attacked them with sticks and vandalized the university's medical center, while JCD Member Secretary Shamsul Arefin denied the claims, accusing the other groups of attempting to create a 'mob situation'.

Jatiya Chhatra Shakti President Shahin Mia reported that he and others were assaulted indiscriminately, while Socialist Students' Front President Ivan Tahsiv criticized the university administration's silence on 'occupational politics'.
University Proctor Prof Nasir Uddin stated that they suspect 'anti-July forces' or banned Chhatra League activists may have been behind the disorder and promised an investigation.
Sutrapur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Matiur Rahman confirmed that the situation on and around the campus has since calmed down.
caption:

The clash broke out around 11:30 am during a documentary screening program attended by University Grants Commission (UGC) Chairman Prof Dr Mamun Ahmed.

The violence started when JCD activists stopped JnUCSU representatives and members of Inquilab Mancha from entering the venue with placards demanding better campus facilities and army oversight of the second campus construction.

Injured individuals include JnUCSU Vice-President Riazul Islam, General Secretary Abdul Alim Arif, Jatiya Chhatra Shakti President Shahin Mia, and JCD leader Yasin Saif.

Abdul Alim Arif alleged that JCD activists attacked them with sticks and vandalized the university's medical center, while JCD Member Secretary Shamsul Arefin denied the claims, accusing the other groups of attempting to create a 'mob situation'.

Jatiya Chhatra Shakti President Shahin Mia reported that he and others were assaulted indiscriminately, while Socialist Students' Front President Ivan Tahsiv criticized the university administration's silence on 'occupational politics'.

University Proctor Prof Nasir Uddin stated that they suspect 'anti-July forces' or banned Chhatra League activists may have been behind the disorder and promised an investigation.

headline_marked: Rail link to north snapped as [[Silk City Express coach derails]] in Sirajganj
headline: Rail link to north snapped as Silk City Express coach derails in Sirajganj
summary: Train services between Dhaka and northern Bangladesh are suspended after a coach derailed near Shaheed M Mansur Ali Railway Station, causing widespread commuter inconvenience.
details: A coach of the Dhaka-bound Silk City Express derailed near Shaheed M Mansur Ali Railway Station in Sirajganj around 10:55 am today. The train, originating from Rajshahi, came to an immediate halt after the emergency brake chain was pulled.
No casualties were reported in the incident, according to the station master of Jamuna Bridge West Railway Station, Md Moniruzzaman.

The derailment has completely suspended all train movement between Dhaka and northern Bangladesh. Services to the south-west were also halted as they rely on the Jamuna Rail Bridge, for which there is no alternative route.
Several trains, including the Nilphamari-bound Nil Sagar Express, have been stranded at various stations along the route, leaving numerous passengers stranded.
Railway authorities have dispatched relief crews and a rescue train to the site to clear the tracks and restore normal services as quickly as possible.
caption:
Rail links between Dhaka and northern Bangladesh have been completely snapped after a train derailment in Sirajganj.

A coach of the Dhaka-bound Silk City Express derailed near Shaheed M Mansur Ali Railway Station in Sirajganj around 10:55 am today. The train, originating from Rajshahi, came to an immediate halt after the emergency brake chain was pulled.

No casualties were reported in the incident, according to the station master of Jamuna Bridge West Railway Station, Md Moniruzzaman.

The derailment has completely suspended all train movement between Dhaka and northern Bangladesh. Services to the south-west were also halted as they rely on the Jamuna Rail Bridge, for which there is no alternative route.

Several trains, including the Nilphamari-bound Nil Sagar Express, have been stranded at various stations along the route, leaving numerous passengers stranded.

Railway authorities have dispatched relief crews and a rescue train to the site to clear the tracks and restore normal services as quickly as possible.
